long_biography.plain_text:
As a child in Buenos Aires, Juan Carlos López Mena sold vegetables from a decorated handcart after illness interrupted his father's work. He later ran a shirt-manufacturing business before turning to Río de la Plata transport. In 1979 he bought an older passenger vessel and created the operation that became Buquebus. The business grew from a river crossing into linked ferry, coach, terminal, tourism and hospitality services between Argentina and Uruguay.

López Mena remains president and the disclosed majority shareholder of Los Cipreses, Buquebus's Uruguayan operator. His continuing ownership and reinvestment make the transport group the clearest basis of his personal fortune, while his operating role remains active. Fleet purchases, terminals, hotels, turnover, debt and loan-backed development projects sit within the company. They should not be counted wholesale as his personal assets, even though his stake gives him the economic exposure of a controlling founder.
